lines: Itu tidak urusan kamu.

why.en: urusan is a noun → a noun is negated with the noun negator, not the verb/adjective one.
why.ko: urusan은 명사 → 명사는 동사·형용사용 부정어로 부정하지 않음.

gloss.en: That's none of your business.

lines: Ini tidak cinta biasa.

why.en: cinta biasa is a noun phrase → nouns take the noun negator.
why.ko: cinta biasa는 명사구 → 명사용 부정어를 씀.

gloss.en: This isn't ordinary love.

lines: Itu tidak sihir, hanya tipuan.

why.en: sihir is a noun → negate it with the noun negator.
why.ko: sihir는 명사 → 명사용 부정어로 부정.

gloss.en: That's not magic, just a trick.

lines: Menyerah tidak pilihan bagiku.

why.en: pilihan is a noun ('an option') → the noun negator goes before it.
why.ko: pilihan은 명사(선택지) → 그 앞엔 명사용 부정어.

gloss.en: Giving up is not an option for me.

lines: Dia tidak tipe orang yang mudah marah.

why.en: tipe orang is a noun phrase → noun negator.
why.ko: tipe orang은 명사구 → 명사용 부정어.

gloss.en: He is not the type who gets angry easily.

lines: Itu bukan adil.

why.en: adil is an adjective → adjectives are negated with the verb/adjective negator.
why.ko: adil은 형용사 → 형용사는 동사·형용사용 부정어로 부정.

gloss.en: That's not fair.

lines: Rekaman itu bukan jelas.

why.en: jelas is an adjective → negate it with the verb/adjective negator.
why.ko: jelas는 형용사 → 동사·형용사용 부정어로 부정.

gloss.en: That recording isn't clear.

lines: Mengganggu orang lain itu bukan sopan.

why.en: sopan is an adjective → adjective negator, not the noun one.
why.ko: sopan은 형용사 → 명사용이 아니라 형용사용 부정어.

gloss.en: Disturbing others is rude.
gloss.ko: 다른 사람을 방해하는 건 예의가 아니다.

lines: Nenek tinggal ke desa.

why.en: tinggal is staying in a place, not moving → location, not direction.
why.ko: tinggal은 이동이 아니라 머무름 → 방향이 아니라 장소 전치사.

gloss.en: Grandma lives in the village.

lines: Mereka duduk ke taman.

why.en: duduk tells where they sit → a place, not a direction.
why.ko: duduk은 앉아 있는 곳을 말함 → 방향이 아니라 장소.

gloss.en: They're sitting in the park.

lines: Kita bertemu ke stasiun.

why.en: Meeting happens at a place → location preposition.
why.ko: 만나는 일은 어떤 장소에서 → 장소 전치사.

gloss.en: We'll meet at the station.

lines: Kami pergi di laut kemarin.

why.en: pergi is movement toward somewhere → direction, not location.
why.ko: pergi는 어딘가로 가는 움직임 → 장소가 아니라 방향 전치사.

gloss.en: We went to the sea yesterday.

lines: Dia pergi di negara lain.

why.en: pergi needs the destination marker, not the 'at' marker.
why.ko: pergi에는 '~에서'가 아니라 도착지 표시가 필요.

gloss.en: He went to another country.

lines: Rumahnya jauh di sini.

why.en: jauh measures distance from a point → the 'from' preposition.
why.ko: jauh는 어떤 지점으로부터의 거리 → '~에서부터' 전치사.

gloss.en: His house is far from here.

lines: Jangan duduk ke tanah.

why.en: duduk says where you sit → location, not direction.
why.ko: duduk은 앉는 곳 → 방향이 아니라 장소.

gloss.en: Don't sit on the ground.

lines: Mahasiswa baru tinggal ke asrama kampus.

why.en: tinggal (live) is about where you are, not where you go.
why.ko: tinggal(살다)은 가는 곳이 아니라 있는 곳.

gloss.en: New students live in the campus dormitory.

lines: Jam apa sekarang?

why.en: Asking the time asks for a number → the 'how many' question word.
why.ko: 시간을 묻는 건 숫자를 묻는 것 → '몇'에 해당하는 의문사.

gloss.en: What time is it now?

lines: Adalah tiga kursi kosong.

why.en: 'There are' is expressed with the existence verb; the formal copula only links a subject to a noun.
why.ko: '~이 있다'는 존재 동사로; 격식 계사는 주어와 명사를 잇기만 함.

gloss.en: There are three empty chairs.

lines: Adalah toko di sekitar sini.

why.en: Saying something exists needs the existence verb, not the copula.
why.ko: 무엇이 있다고 말할 땐 계사가 아니라 존재 동사.

gloss.en: There's a shop around here.

lines: Siapa yang mempanggil?

why.en: With me-, a root starting with p loses that first p.
why.ko: me-가 붙으면 p로 시작하는 어근의 첫 p가 떨어짐.

gloss.en: Who's calling?

lines: Aku sudah mempilih yang ini.

why.en: Root pilih starts with p → the p melts into the prefix.
why.ko: 어근 pilih는 p로 시작 → p가 접두사에 녹아 사라짐.

gloss.en: I've already chosen this one.

lines: Mereka suka mentolong orang lain.

why.en: Root tolong starts with t → t drops after men-.
why.ko: 어근 tolong은 t로 시작 → men- 뒤에서 t가 떨어짐.

gloss.en: They like helping other people.

lines: Dia suka mentonton berita.

why.en: t at the start of the root disappears after the me- prefix.
why.ko: 어근 첫 t는 me- 접두사 뒤에서 사라짐.

gloss.en: He likes watching the news.

lines: Dia suka mentulis cerita.

why.en: Root tulis: the initial t is replaced by the nasal.
why.ko: 어근 tulis: 첫 t가 비음으로 바뀜.

gloss.en: She likes writing stories.

lines: Dia mensimpan uang di bank.

why.en: Root simpan: initial s becomes ny- with me-.
why.ko: 어근 simpan: 첫 s는 me-와 만나 ny-가 됨.

gloss.en: He keeps money in the bank.

lines: Aku benci mentunggu lama.

why.en: Root tunggu: initial t drops after men-.
why.ko: 어근 tunggu: 첫 t가 men- 뒤에서 떨어짐.

gloss.en: I hate waiting a long time.

lines: Kakek selalu mempakai sarung di rumah.

why.en: Root pakai: initial p drops after mem-.
why.ko: 어근 pakai: 첫 p가 mem- 뒤에서 떨어짐.

gloss.en: Grandfather always wears a sarong at home.

lines: Ibu berbuat kue.

why.en: Making a cake has an object → the transitive me- verb, not the intransitive ber- one ('to act').
why.ko: 케이크를 만든다는 목적어가 있음 → 자동사 ber-('행동하다')가 아니라 타동사 me-.

gloss.en: Mom's making cake.

lines: Nomor teleponku mengubah.

why.en: The number changes by itself, with no object → intransitive ber- verb.
why.ko: 번호가 스스로 바뀜, 목적어 없음 → 자동사 ber- 동사.

gloss.en: My phone number changed.

lines: Mobil itu mulai menggerak.

why.en: The car moves by itself → ber- verb; the me- form needs -kan and an object.
why.ko: 차가 스스로 움직임 → ber- 동사; me- 꼴은 -kan과 목적어가 필요.

gloss.en: That car started moving.

lines: Hujan menghenti tadi.

why.en: The rain stops on its own → ber- verb, no object.
why.ko: 비가 저절로 그침 → 목적어 없는 ber- 동사.

gloss.en: The rain stopped earlier.

lines: Filmnya mengakhir sedih.

why.en: The film ends by itself → intransitive ber- verb.
why.ko: 영화가 저절로 끝남 → 자동사 ber- 동사.

gloss.en: The movie ended sadly.

lines: Jangan membicara keras-keras.

why.en: 'Talk' with no object is a ber- verb; the me- form needs -kan and a topic.
why.ko: 목적어 없는 '말하다'는 ber- 동사; me- 꼴은 -kan과 대상이 필요.

gloss.en: Don't talk loudly.

lines: Ayo memain di luar.

why.en: 'Play' without an object takes ber-.
why.ko: 목적어 없는 '놀다'는 ber-.

gloss.en: Let's play outside.

lines: Aku harus berlajar malam ini.

why.en: This verb's prefix is irregular: before -ajar it is bel-, not ber-.
why.ko: 이 동사의 접두사는 불규칙: -ajar 앞에선 ber-가 아니라 bel-.

gloss.en: I have to study tonight.

lines: Besok kita menemu lagi.

why.en: Meeting each other has no object → ber- verb.
why.ko: 서로 만나는 건 목적어가 없음 → ber- 동사.

gloss.en: We'll meet again tomorrow.

lines: Kami menghasil berkat bantuan teman.

why.en: 'Succeed' is intransitive → ber-; the me- form means 'produce' and needs -kan.
why.ko: '성공하다'는 자동사 → ber-; me- 꼴은 '생산하다'이고 -kan이 필요.

gloss.en: We succeeded thanks to our friends' help.

lines: Tolong aku ikut?

why.en: Asking permission for yourself → the 'may' word; the other one asks someone else to do something.
why.ko: 내가 해도 되는지 묻기 → '해도 된다' 말; 다른 말은 남에게 해 달라고 부탁할 때.

gloss.en: Can I come along?

lines: Tolong aku bertanya?

why.en: The speaker wants to ask → asking permission, not requesting help.
why.ko: 말하는 사람이 묻고 싶음 → 도움 부탁이 아니라 허락 구하기.

gloss.en: May I ask?

lines: Acara memulai pukul tujuh malam.

why.en: The event doesn't start something else; it is started → passive.
why.ko: 행사가 무언가를 시작하는 게 아니라 시작됨 → 수동.

gloss.en: The event starts at seven in the evening.

lines: Keputusan akhirnya sudah membuat.

why.en: The decision is what gets made → passive, not active.
why.ko: 결정은 만들어지는 대상 → 능동이 아니라 수동.

gloss.en: The final decision has been made.

lines: Bahasa Indonesia mudah mempelajari.

why.en: The language is what is learned, not the learner → passive after mudah.
why.ko: 언어는 배우는 쪽이 아니라 배워지는 대상 → mudah 뒤에 수동.

gloss.en: Indonesian is easy to learn.

lines: Teori ini sulit memahami.

why.en: The theory is the thing understood → passive after sulit.
why.ko: 이론은 이해되는 대상 → sulit 뒤에 수동.

gloss.en: This theory is hard to understand.

lines: Kuliah hari ini membatalkan.

why.en: The lecture is cancelled by someone → passive.
why.ko: 강의는 누군가에 의해 취소됨 → 수동.

gloss.en: Today's lecture was canceled.

lines: Kemenangan itu merayakan meriah.

why.en: A victory can't celebrate; it is celebrated → passive.
why.ko: 승리가 축하할 수는 없음, 축하받음 → 수동.

gloss.en: That victory was celebrated grandly.

lines: Mobilnya memarkir di dalam garasi.

why.en: The car is parked by someone → passive.
why.ko: 차는 누군가에 의해 주차됨 → 수동.

gloss.en: His car is parked inside the garage.
gloss.ko: 그의 차는 차고 안에 주차되어 있다.

lines: Izin masuknya sudah menyetujui.

why.en: The permit is what gets approved → passive.
why.ko: 허가는 승인되는 대상 → 수동.

gloss.en: His entry permit has been approved.

lines: Toilet umum di stasiun sedang membersihkan.

why.en: The toilet is being cleaned, it isn't cleaning → passive.
why.ko: 화장실이 청소하는 게 아니라 청소되는 중 → 수동.

gloss.en: The public toilet at the station is being cleaned.

lines: Kami menjebak di lift.

why.en: Being stuck happened to us, with no object → ter- for an unintended state.
why.ko: 갇힌 건 우리에게 일어난 일, 목적어 없음 → 뜻하지 않은 상태의 ter-.

gloss.en: We're stuck in the elevator.

lines: Rotinya hampir membakar.

why.en: The bread didn't burn something; it got burnt by accident → ter-.
why.ko: 빵이 무언가를 태운 게 아니라 실수로 타 버림 → ter-.

gloss.en: The bread almost burned.

lines: Dia membangun karena suara petir.

why.en: Waking up because of a noise is involuntary → ter-; the me- form means 'build'.
why.ko: 소리 때문에 깬 건 뜻하지 않은 일 → ter-; me- 꼴은 '짓다'.

gloss.en: He woke up because of the thunder.

lines: Buku itu menjatuh dari rak yang tinggi.

why.en: The book fell by accident → ter-; a me- form would need -kan and an object.
why.ko: 책이 실수로 떨어짐 → ter-; me- 꼴은 -kan과 목적어가 필요.

gloss.en: That book fell from the high shelf.

lines: Kereta malam cenderung paling sepi daripada kereta siang.

why.en: A comparison with daripada (than) needs the comparative word, not the superlative.
why.ko: daripada(~보다)가 있는 비교 → 최상급이 아니라 비교급 말.

gloss.en: Night trains tend to be quieter than daytime trains.
gloss.ko: 밤 기차는 낮 기차보다 한산한 편이다.

lines: Ternyata mengurus izin usaha paling repot daripada membuat aplikasinya.

why.en: Two things are compared with daripada → comparative, not superlative.
why.ko: daripada로 두 가지를 비교 → 최상급이 아니라 비교급.

gloss.en: It turned out that getting a business permit was more of a hassle than building the app.
gloss.ko: 알고 보니 사업 허가를 받는 게 앱을 만드는 것보다 더 번거로웠다.

lines: Kardus bekas toko elektronik terbukti paling kuat daripada kardus biasa.

why.en: daripada compares two kinds of box → comparative word.
why.ko: daripada로 두 종류의 상자를 비교 → 비교급 말.

gloss.en: Boxes from the electronics store proved to be sturdier than ordinary boxes.
gloss.ko: 전자제품 가게의 헌 상자가 보통 상자보다 더 튼튼한 것으로 드러났다.

lines: Eko paling suka memerankan komedi daripada drama yang serius.

why.en: Preferring one thing over another with daripada → comparative.
why.ko: daripada로 하나를 다른 것보다 좋아함 → 비교급.

gloss.en: Eko prefers acting in comedies over serious dramas.
gloss.ko: 에코는 진지한 드라마보다 코미디 연기를 더 좋아한다.

lines: Aku menemui kuncimu.

why.en: Finding a thing takes -kan; the -i form means meeting a person.
why.ko: 물건을 찾아내는 건 -kan; -i 꼴은 사람을 만나다.

gloss.en: I found your keys.

lines: Kami membutuh waktu lebih.

why.en: This verb only exists with the -kan suffix.
why.ko: 이 동사는 -kan 접미사가 있어야만 쓰임.

gloss.en: We need more time.

lines: Aku tidak melaku apa-apa.

why.en: 'Do' as a transitive me- verb needs -kan.
why.ko: 타동사 '하다'의 me- 꼴은 -kan이 필요.

gloss.en: I didn't do anything.

lines: Jangan melupa janji kita.

why.en: Forgetting something (an object) needs the -kan suffix here.
why.ko: 무언가(목적어)를 잊는 건 여기서 -kan이 필요.

gloss.en: Don't forget our promise.

lines: Dia menyuka film lama.

why.en: 'Like' with an object needs the -i suffix.
why.ko: 목적어가 있는 '좋아하다'는 -i가 필요.

gloss.en: She likes old movies.

lines: Kami membicara rencana itu.

why.en: Discussing a topic (object) needs me- … -kan.
why.ko: 어떤 주제(목적어)를 논의하는 건 me-…-kan.

gloss.en: We talked about that plan.

lines: Aku mengunjung nenek setiap minggu.

why.en: Visiting someone needs the -i suffix with its object.
why.ko: 누군가를 방문하는 건 목적어와 함께 -i가 필요.

gloss.en: I visit grandma every week.

lines: Dia akan menghadir upacara di balai kota.

why.en: Attending an event (object) needs -i.
why.ko: 행사(목적어)에 참석하는 건 -i가 필요.

gloss.en: She will attend the ceremony at city hall.
gloss.ko: 그는 시청에서 열리는 식에 참석할 것이다.

lines: Tunjukkan identitas sebelum memasukkan gedung.

why.en: Entering a building takes -i; the -kan form means putting something in.
why.ko: 건물에 들어가는 건 -i; -kan 꼴은 무언가를 넣다.

gloss.en: Show your identity before entering the building.
gloss.ko: 건물에 들어가기 전에 신분증을 보여 주세요.

lines: Perkenalkan teman saya siapa baru pindah ke sini.

why.en: A relative clause after a noun is joined with the relative word, not a question word.
why.ko: 명사 뒤 관계절은 의문사가 아니라 관계사로 잇는다.

gloss.en: Let me introduce my friend who just moved here.
gloss.ko: 얼마 전에 이리로 이사 온 내 친구를 소개할게.

lines: Hanya orang tertentu siapa boleh masuk.

why.en: 'Only certain people who…' is a relative clause → relative word, not a question word.
why.ko: '~하는 특정한 사람만'은 관계절 → 의문사가 아니라 관계사.

gloss.en: Only certain people may enter.

lines: Jangan menghina orang siapa sedang kesulitan.

why.en: Describing which people with a clause → relative word, not 'who?'.
why.ko: 어떤 사람인지 절로 꾸밈 → '누구?'가 아니라 관계사.

gloss.en: Do not insult people who are struggling.

lines: Menuruti Intan, kelebihan kereta adalah bisa tidur sambil berjalan.

why.en: 'According to X' is the bare form; the -i verb means 'to obey'.
why.ko: 'X에 따르면'은 맨 꼴; -i가 붙으면 '따르다(복종)'.

gloss.en: According to Intan, the advantage of the train is that you can sleep while traveling.
gloss.ko: 인탄에 따르면 기차의 장점은 이동하면서 잘 수 있다는 것이다.

lines: Menuruti Eko, kasur di rumah sewaan itu agak keras, tapi dia tetap tidur nyenyak.

why.en: Giving someone's opinion uses the bare form, not the verb 'obey'.
why.ko: 누군가의 의견을 전할 땐 '복종하다' 동사가 아니라 맨 꼴.

gloss.en: According to Eko, the mattress in the rented house was a bit hard, but he still slept soundly.
gloss.ko: 에코에 따르면 셋집 매트리스는 좀 딱딱했지만 그는 푹 잤다.

lines: Dia menunjukkan berani di saat sulit.

why.en: menunjukkan needs a noun object → the ke-…-an noun, not the bare adjective.
why.ko: menunjukkan에는 명사 목적어가 필요 → 맨 형용사가 아니라 ke-…-an 명사.

gloss.en: She showed courage in a difficult moment.
gloss.ko: 그는 어려운 순간에 용기를 보여 주었다.

lines: Mereka menghadapi sulit keuangan.

why.en: After menghadapi comes a thing faced → noun (ke-…-an), not adjective.
why.ko: menghadapi 뒤엔 마주한 대상 → 형용사가 아니라 ke-…-an 명사.

gloss.en: They are facing financial difficulties.

lines: Intan membeli kursi kerja baru demi nyaman para programmer.

why.en: demi ('for the sake of') is followed by a noun → ke-…-an noun.
why.ko: demi(~를 위해) 뒤에는 명사 → ke-…-an 명사.

gloss.en: Intan bought new office chairs for the programmers' comfort.
gloss.ko: 인탄은 프로그래머들의 편안함을 위해 새 업무용 의자를 샀다.

lines: Jangan melakukan hewan dengan kasar.

why.en: 'Treat (someone) a certain way' is the memper-…-kan verb; the shorter one only means 'do'.
why.ko: '(누구를) 어떻게 대하다'는 memper-…-kan 동사; 짧은 꼴은 '하다'일 뿐.

gloss.en: Don't treat animals roughly.

lines: Dia sedang membaik sepeda.

why.en: Fixing a bicycle (object) needs memper-…-i; the me- form means 'get better' by itself.
why.ko: 자전거(목적어)를 고치는 건 memper-…-i; me- 꼴은 저절로 '나아지다'.

gloss.en: He's fixing the bicycle.

lines: Mereka membaik atap sebelum musim hujan.

why.en: Repairing the roof is done to an object → memper-…-i, not 'improve' on its own.
why.ko: 지붕 수리는 목적어에 하는 일 → 혼자 '나아지다'가 아니라 memper-…-i.

gloss.en: They repaired the roof before the rainy season.

lines: Mereka menjuangkan kebebasan rakyat.

why.en: 'Fight for' is built with memper-…-kan; there is no plain me- form.
why.ko: '~를 위해 싸우다'는 memper-…-kan으로; 그냥 me- 꼴은 없음.

gloss.en: They fight for the people's freedom.

lines: Hujan turun terus-menerus sejak pagi supaya Dimas batal bersepeda.

why.en: Rain has no intention; cancelling the ride is a result → result connector.
why.ko: 비에는 의도가 없음; 자전거를 못 탄 건 결과 → 결과 접속사.

gloss.en: It rained nonstop since the morning, so Dimas canceled his bike ride.
gloss.ko: 아침부터 비가 계속 내려서 디마스는 자전거 타기를 취소했다.

lines: Hijau ada warna favoritku.

why.en: Linking a subject to a noun ('is') uses the copula; the existence verb means 'there is'.
why.ko: 주어와 명사를 잇는 '~이다'는 계사; 존재 동사는 '~이 있다'.

gloss.en: Green is my favorite color.

lines: Musik ada hiburan favoritnya setelah kerja.

why.en: 'Music is his entertainment' links two nouns → copula, not 'there is'.
why.ko: '음악은 그의 오락이다'는 두 명사를 이음 → '있다'가 아니라 계사.

gloss.en: Music is her favorite entertainment after work.
gloss.ko: 음악은 그가 일한 뒤 가장 좋아하는 오락이다.

lines: Seni lukis ada hobinya sejak kecil.

why.en: Identifying what her hobby is → copula between nouns.
why.ko: 그의 취미가 무엇인지 밝힘 → 명사 사이의 계사.

gloss.en: Painting has been his hobby since childhood.
gloss.ko: 그림 그리기는 어릴 때부터 그의 취미였다.

lines: Wati ada pewaris biola tua milik kakeknya.

why.en: Saying who someone is (an heir) → copula, not existence.
why.ko: 누가 무엇인지(상속자) 말함 → 존재가 아니라 계사.

gloss.en: Wati is the heir to her grandfather's old violin.
gloss.ko: 와티는 할아버지의 낡은 바이올린을 물려받은 사람이다.

lines: Jam tangan Agus ada pemberian kakeknya saat dia masuk SMA.

why.en: The watch is identified as a gift → copula, not 'there is'.
why.ko: 시계가 선물임을 밝힘 → '있다'가 아니라 계사.

gloss.en: Agus's watch was a gift from his grandfather when he started high school.
gloss.ko: 아구스의 손목시계는 그가 고등학교에 들어갈 때 할아버지가 준 선물이다.

lines: Bantu aku kok.

why.en: A friendly request is softened with the request particle; the other one shows surprise.
why.ko: 다정한 부탁은 부탁용 소사로 부드럽게; 다른 소사는 놀람을 나타냄.

gloss.en: Help me, will you?

lines: Dong kamu terlambat lagi?

why.en: A surprised 'how come…?' question opens with the surprise particle; the other is for requests.
why.ko: 놀라서 묻는 '어째서…?'는 놀람 소사로 시작; 다른 소사는 부탁용.

gloss.en: How come you're late again?

lines: Instruktur meminta Andi mengukus labu sampai keras untuk sup.

why.en: Steaming makes pumpkin soft, and soup needs it soft → the result can't be hard.
why.ko: 찌면 호박이 물러지고 수프에도 물러야 함 → 딱딱해질 수 없음.

gloss.en: The instructor asked Andi to steam the pumpkin until soft for the soup.
gloss.ko: 강사는 안디에게 수프에 쓸 호박을 무를 때까지 찌라고 했다.

lines: Fajar menunggu sampai pisang di raknya benar-benar mentah untuk dibuat bolu.

why.en: You wait for bananas to change, and cake needs soft sweet ones → he waited for ripeness, not rawness.
why.ko: 바나나가 변하길 기다리고, 케이크엔 물렁하고 단 게 필요 → 덜 익음이 아니라 익기를 기다림.

gloss.en: Fajar waits until the bananas on his shelf are fully ripe to make sponge cake.
gloss.ko: 파자르는 바나나 케이크를 만들려고 선반의 바나나가 완전히 익을 때까지 기다린다.

lines: Dimas mengatur beban di rak supaya miring dan tidak mudah roboh.

why.en: He arranges the load so the shelf won't fall → he wants it even, not tilted.
why.ko: 선반이 쓰러지지 않게 짐을 정리함 → 기울게가 아니라 고르게.

gloss.en: Dimas arranges the load on the shelf so it is balanced and won't topple easily.
gloss.ko: 디마스는 선반의 짐을 균형 있게 놓아 쉽게 쓰러지지 않게 한다.

lines: Setelah mencicipi semua masakan teman sekelas, Andi sudah terlalu lapar untuk makan siang.

why.en: After tasting every dish, someone who can't eat lunch is too full, not too hungry.
why.ko: 모든 음식을 맛본 뒤 점심을 못 먹는다면 → 배고파서가 아니라 너무 배불러서.

gloss.en: After tasting all his classmates' dishes, Andi was too full for lunch.
gloss.ko: 반 친구들 음식을 다 맛본 뒤 안디는 너무 배불러서 점심을 먹을 수 없었다.

lines: Ayu menangis begitu pelan sampai seisi ruang tunggu menoleh.

why.en: The whole waiting room turned to look → the crying must have been loud.
why.ko: 대기실 사람들이 모두 돌아봄 → 울음이 컸을 것.

gloss.en: Ayu cried so loudly that everyone in the waiting room turned around.
gloss.ko: 아유가 너무 크게 울어서 대기실 사람들이 모두 돌아보았다.

lead: Mobil-mobil tidak bisa lewat karena air setinggi lutut di jalan.
lines: Akibat hujan deras, jalanan kering.

why.en: Knee-deep water after heavy rain → the street can't be dry.
why.ko: 폭우 뒤 물이 무릎까지 참 → 길이 말라 있을 수 없음.

gloss.en: As a result of heavy rain, the streets flooded.

lead: Sejak pagi langit gelap dan angin bertiup sangat kencang.
lines: Mereka membatalkan piknik karena cuaca cerah.

why.en: A dark, very windy sky and a cancelled picnic → the weather wasn't fine.
why.ko: 어둡고 바람 센 하늘, 취소된 소풍 → 날씨가 좋았을 리 없음.

gloss.en: They canceled the picnic because of bad weather.

lead: Perusahaan lama Rina tutup, dan semua karyawannya kehilangan pekerjaan.
lines: Rina pindah ke kantor ini karena perusahaan lamanya sukses.

why.en: The old company shut down and everyone lost their jobs → it didn't do well.
why.ko: 옛 회사가 문을 닫고 모두 일자리를 잃음 → 잘됐을 리 없음.

gloss.en: Rina moved to this office because her old company went bankrupt.
gloss.ko: 리나는 예전 회사가 파산해서 이 사무실로 옮겼다.

lead: Malam itu topi orang-orang terbang dan pohon kelapa bergoyang keras.
lines: Pesta kembang api batal karena angin terlalu lemah.

why.en: Hats flying and palm trees swaying hard → the wind was the strong kind that stops fireworks.
why.ko: 모자가 날아가고 야자수가 세게 흔들림 → 불꽃놀이를 막을 만큼 센 바람.

gloss.en: The fireworks were cancelled because the wind was too strong.
gloss.ko: 바람이 너무 세서 불꽃놀이 축제가 취소되었다.

lead: Di desa pegunungan itu, warga memakai baju hangat bahkan pada siang hari.
lines: Rudi membawa jaket tebal karena iklim di pegunungan ini panas sepanjang tahun.

why.en: Thick jacket, and locals wear warm clothes even at noon → the climate is cool.
why.ko: 두꺼운 재킷, 주민들이 한낮에도 따뜻하게 입음 → 기후가 서늘함.

gloss.en: Rudi brought a thick jacket because the climate in these mountains is cool all year.
gloss.ko: 이 산지는 일 년 내내 서늘해서 루디는 두꺼운 재킷을 가져갔다.

lead: Pohon di puncak itu tidak ada yang lebih tinggi dari pinggang orang dewasa.
lines: Di puncak gunung hanya tumbuh pohon-pohon besar karena anginnya kencang.

why.en: Trees no taller than a person's waist in strong wind → they are stunted.
why.ko: 센 바람 속 사람 허리보다 낮은 나무 → 작게 자란 나무.

gloss.en: Only stunted trees grow on the mountaintop because the wind is strong.
gloss.ko: 산꼭대기에는 바람이 세서 키 작은 나무들만 자란다.

lead: Dari pinggir kolam, Rina bisa melihat koin kecil di lantai kolam.
lines: Air di kolam renang itu keruh sekali sampai dasarnya kelihatan.

why.en: You can see a small coin on the bottom → the water is clear.
why.ko: 바닥의 작은 동전이 보임 → 물이 맑음.

gloss.en: The water in that pool is so clear you can see the bottom.
gloss.ko: 그 수영장 물은 바닥이 보일 만큼 아주 맑다.

lead: Sejak pagi mesin-mesin besar berbunyi keras di jalan depan apotek Wati.
lines: Wati sulit mendengar pelanggan karena ketenangan proyek jalan di depan apotek.

why.en: Big machines roaring all morning and she can't hear customers → it's noise, not quiet.
why.ko: 큰 기계가 아침 내내 시끄럽고 손님 말이 안 들림 → 고요가 아니라 소음.

gloss.en: Wati finds it hard to hear customers because of the noise from the roadworks in front of the pharmacy.
gloss.ko: 와티는 약국 앞 도로 공사 소음 때문에 손님 말을 듣기 어렵다.

lead: Malam itu semua kamar hotel di desa sudah dipesan orang lain.
lines: Bayu memutuskan bermalam di rumah warga karena hotel sudah kosong.

why.en: Every room was booked, so he stayed with locals → the hotel had no space.
why.ko: 방이 모두 예약돼 주민 집에서 잠 → 호텔에 자리가 없었음.

gloss.en: Bayu decided to spend the night at a local's house because the hotels were full.
gloss.ko: 호텔이 다 차서 바유는 주민 집에서 하룻밤 묵기로 했다.

lead: Setiap kali Budi duduk, kaki kursinya berbunyi dan hampir lepas.
lines: Kursi Budi sudah kokoh, jadi ia minta ganti ke penjaga sekolah.

why.en: The chair creaks and a leg nearly comes off → it's wobbly, so he asks for a new one.
why.ko: 의자가 삐걱대고 다리가 빠질 듯함 → 흔들리니 바꿔 달라고 함.

gloss.en: Budi's chair was wobbly, so he asked the school caretaker for a new one.
gloss.ko: 부디의 의자가 흔들려서 그는 학교 관리인에게 바꿔 달라고 했다.

lead: Lantai toilet itu penuh lumpur dan baunya tidak enak.
lines: Toilet portabel di dekat garis start sangat bersih, jadi Siti menahan diri.

why.en: Mud on the floor and a bad smell, so she held on → the toilet was dirty.
why.ko: 바닥에 진흙과 나쁜 냄새, 그래서 참음 → 화장실이 더러웠음.

gloss.en: The portable toilets near the start line were very dirty, so Siti held it in.
gloss.ko: 출발선 근처 이동식 화장실이 너무 더러워서 시티는 참았다.

lead: Agus membaca halaman yang sama berkali-kali, tetapi tetap tidak paham.
lines: Agus mudah berkonsentrasi karena suara bor dari gedung sebelah.

why.en: He reread the same page and still didn't get it → concentrating was hard.
why.ko: 같은 쪽을 거듭 읽어도 이해 못 함 → 집중하기 어려웠음.

gloss.en: Agus found it hard to concentrate because of the drilling from the next building.
gloss.ko: 아구스는 옆 건물의 드릴 소리 때문에 집중하기 어렵다.

lead: Ponsel Dewi tiba-tiba padam dan tidak bisa dinyalakan lagi.
lines: Dewi mencari bilik telepon di stasiun karena baterai ponselnya penuh.

why.en: Her phone went dead and won't turn on → the battery was empty.
why.ko: 휴대폰이 꺼지고 안 켜짐 → 배터리가 바닥남.

gloss.en: Dewi looked for a phone booth at the station because her phone battery was dead.
gloss.ko: 데위는 휴대폰 배터리가 다 닳아서 역에서 공중전화 부스를 찾았다.

lead: Intan hampir tidak bisa mengangkat kopernya sendiri.
lines: Intan memakai jasa porter karena kopernya terlalu ringan.

why.en: She could barely lift it herself and hired a porter → the suitcase was heavy.
why.ko: 혼자 거의 못 들고 짐꾼을 씀 → 가방이 무거웠음.

gloss.en: Intan used a porter service because her suitcase was too heavy.
gloss.ko: 인탄은 가방이 너무 무거워서 짐꾼 서비스를 이용했다.

lead: Hari itu laut bergelora dan perahu-perahu terombang-ambing.
lines: Dua perahu nelayan hampir bertabrakan di dekat dermaga karena ombak rendah.

why.en: A rough sea tossing the boats → the waves were big.
why.ko: 거친 바다가 배를 흔듦 → 파도가 컸음.

gloss.en: Two fishing boats nearly collided near the pier because of high waves.
gloss.ko: 파도가 높아서 어선 두 척이 부두 근처에서 부딪칠 뻔했다.

lead: Setiap akhir pekan, mal di kota Wati penuh sesak.
lines: Wati lebih suka belanja daring karena malas menghadapi kesunyian mal di akhir pekan.

why.en: The mall is packed every weekend and she avoids it → it's the crowds she dislikes.
why.ko: 주말마다 쇼핑몰이 꽉 차고 그녀는 피함 → 싫은 건 붐빔.

gloss.en: Wati prefers shopping online because she can't be bothered with the weekend crowds at the mall.
gloss.ko: 와티는 주말 쇼핑몰의 북적임을 견디기 싫어서 온라인 쇼핑을 더 좋아한다.

lead: Dari sana Rudi bisa melihat ribuan bintang dengan jelas.
lines: Langit malam di sana sangat berkabut karena atmosfer di pegunungan bebas polusi.

why.en: Thousands of stars seen clearly, pollution-free air → the sky is clear.
why.ko: 수천 개 별이 또렷하고 공기에 오염이 없음 → 하늘이 맑음.

gloss.en: The night sky there is very clear because the mountain atmosphere is free of pollution.
gloss.ko: 산의 공기가 오염이 없어서 그곳 밤하늘은 아주 맑다.

lead: Putri ingin membaca, tetapi lampu di ruangan itu rusak.
lines: Putri berpindah ke kursi dekat jendela supaya lebih gelap.

why.en: She wants to read and the lamp is broken → she moves to the window for light.
why.ko: 책을 읽고 싶은데 전등이 고장 → 빛을 얻으려 창가로 감.

gloss.en: Putri moved to the seat by the window so it would be brighter.
gloss.ko: 푸트리는 더 밝게 하려고 창가 자리로 옮겼다.

lead: Gudang itu hanya lima menit jalan kaki dari rumah Wati.
lines: Gudang penjual itu berjauhan dengan rumah Wati, jadi paketnya sampai dalam sehari.

why.en: Five minutes' walk away and the parcel arrives in a day → the warehouse is near.
why.ko: 걸어서 오 분이고 소포가 하루 만에 옴 → 창고가 가까움.

gloss.en: The seller's warehouse is near Wati's house, so the package arrived within a day.
gloss.ko: 판매자의 창고가 와티의 집과 가까워서 소포가 하루 만에 도착한다.

lead: Dulu warga desa Eko masih memakai lampu minyak dan berjalan di jalan tanah.
lines: Dulu desa Eko dianggap maju karena belum punya listrik dan jalan aspal.

why.en: Oil lamps, dirt roads, no electricity → the village was seen as backward.
why.ko: 등잔불, 흙길, 전기 없음 → 마을이 뒤처졌다고 여겨짐.

gloss.en: Eko's village used to be considered backward because it had no electricity or paved road.
gloss.ko: 예전에 에코의 마을은 전기와 포장도로가 없어서 낙후되었다고 여겨졌다.

lead: Rudi hanya membayar sedikit uang untuk masuk ke museum itu.
lines: Museum kecil di kota Rudi patut dikunjungi karena tiketnya mahal dan koleksinya lengkap.

why.en: He paid only a little to get in → the ticket is cheap.
why.ko: 들어가는 데 돈을 조금만 냄 → 표가 쌈.

gloss.en: The small museum in Rudi's town is worth visiting because tickets are cheap and the collection is complete.
gloss.ko: 루디네 도시의 작은 박물관은 표가 싸고 소장품이 풍부해서 가 볼 만하다.

lead: Siti ingin udara segar masuk ke dalam rumah.
lines: Rumah baru itu masih menyimpan aroma cat yang tajam, jadi Siti menutup semua jendela.

why.en: A sharp paint smell and she wants fresh air → she'd let air in through the windows.
why.ko: 페인트 냄새가 독하고 신선한 공기를 원함 → 창으로 공기를 들여야 함.

gloss.en: The new house still had a sharp smell of paint, so Siti opened all the windows.
gloss.ko: 새 집에 아직 페인트 냄새가 독해서 시티는 창문을 모두 열었다.

lead: Budi tidak mengangkat kepala dari surat itu selama berjam-jam.
lines: Budi begitu bosan membaca surat itu sampai lupa makan malam.

why.en: He didn't look up for hours and forgot dinner → he was absorbed, not bored.
why.ko: 몇 시간이나 고개를 안 들고 저녁을 잊음 → 지루한 게 아니라 푹 빠짐.

gloss.en: Budi was so absorbed in reading the letter that he forgot dinner.
gloss.ko: 부디는 그 편지를 읽는 데 너무 빠져서 저녁 먹는 것도 잊었다.

lead: Wajah Rudi merah dan suaranya makin keras.
lines: Rudi merasa senang karena kakaknya terus memotong penjelasannya.

why.en: Red face, voice getting louder, and being cut off again and again → he was annoyed, not pleased.
why.ko: 얼굴이 빨개지고 목소리가 커짐, 계속 말이 끊김 → 기쁜 게 아니라 짜증남.

gloss.en: Rudi felt frustrated because his sister kept cutting off his explanation.
gloss.ko: 루디는 누나가 계속 설명을 끊어서 답답했다.

lead: Rina menggerutu sambil membersihkan lensa kameranya.
lines: Rina gembira karena pasir masuk ke dalam tas kameranya.

why.en: She grumbles while cleaning sand off her lens → she was irritated.
why.ko: 렌즈의 모래를 닦으며 투덜댐 → 짜증났음.

gloss.en: Rina was annoyed because sand got into her camera bag.
gloss.ko: 리나는 카메라 가방에 모래가 들어가서 짜증이 났다.

lead: Tanah sawah paman Dimas retak-retak dan padinya menguning.
lines: Sawah milik paman Dimas basah berminggu-minggu karena hujan tak kunjung turun.

why.en: Cracked soil, yellowing rice, and rain never came → the field was dry.
why.ko: 땅이 갈라지고 벼가 누렇고 비가 오지 않음 → 논이 말랐음.

gloss.en: Dimas's uncle's rice field stayed dry for weeks because the rain never came.
gloss.ko: 비가 좀처럼 오지 않아 디마스 삼촌의 논은 몇 주째 말라 있다.

lead: Hampir semua murid mendapat nilai jelek di ulangan kimia.
lines: Banyak murid beranggapan pelajaran kimia itu mudah, padahal Andi menyukainya.

why.en: Almost everyone failed the test, and 'whereas Andi likes it' sets him apart → the others think the subject is hard.
why.ko: 거의 모두 시험을 망쳤고 '그런데 안디는 좋아함'이 대조 → 다른 학생들은 어렵다고 여김.

gloss.en: Many students assume chemistry is hard, but Andi likes it.
gloss.ko: 많은 학생이 화학이 어렵다고 생각하지만 안디는 화학을 좋아한다.

lead: Rumah Siti hanya punya satu kamar tidur dan dapur kecil.
lines: Rumahnya memang besar, tapi toh cukup untuk Siti sekeluarga.

why.en: One bedroom and a small kitchen, and 'but it's still enough' answers a drawback → the house is small.
why.ko: 침실 하나와 작은 부엌, '그래도 충분하다'는 단점에 대한 말 → 집이 작음.

gloss.en: The house is small, but it's enough for Siti's family anyway.
gloss.ko: 그 집은 작긴 하지만 그래도 시티 가족에게는 충분하다.

lead: Jalan-jalan di kota itu penuh orang dari kampung lain.
lines: Berita bilang populasi kota turun karena banyak pemudik datang untuk tahun baru.

why.en: The streets are full of people from other villages coming in → the number went up.
why.ko: 다른 마을 사람들이 몰려와 거리가 꽉 참 → 인구가 늘었음.

gloss.en: The news said the city's population went up because many travelers came home for the new year.
gloss.ko: 뉴스에 따르면 새해를 맞아 귀성객이 많이 와서 도시 인구가 늘었다.

lead: Aku pulang tanpa payung, dan air menetes dari rambutku.
lines: Bajuku kering karena hujan deras.

why.en: No umbrella in heavy rain, water dripping from my hair → my clothes got wet.
why.ko: 폭우에 우산 없이 와서 머리에서 물이 떨어짐 → 옷이 젖었음.

gloss.en: My clothes are wet from the heavy rain.

lead: Ibu berbisik, "Ssst, bayinya baru saja tidur."
lines: Bicara keras agar bayi tidak bangun.

why.en: The baby has just fallen asleep and Mum is whispering → talk quietly.
why.ko: 아기가 막 잠들었고 엄마가 속삭임 → 조용히 말해야 함.

gloss.en: Speak softly so the baby doesn't wake.

lead: Aku baru belajar bahasa ini dan masih sering bingung.
lines: Bicara cepat-cepat agar aku mengerti.

why.en: I've only just started and get confused → I need slow speech to understand.
why.ko: 막 배우기 시작해서 자주 헷갈림 → 이해하려면 천천히 말해 줘야 함.

gloss.en: Speak slowly so I can understand.

lead: Seprai di motel itu putih dan lantainya mengilap.
lines: Motel itu kotor meski harganya murah.

why.en: White sheets and shiny floors → the motel is clean, which is surprising for the low price.
why.ko: 하얀 시트와 반짝이는 바닥 → 모텔이 깨끗함, 싼 값에 비해 놀라움.

gloss.en: That motel is clean even though the price is low.

lead: Matahari keluar lagi dan langit menjadi biru.
lines: Cuaca memburuk setelah badai berlalu.

why.en: The sun is out and the sky is blue again → the weather got better.
why.ko: 해가 다시 나오고 하늘이 파래짐 → 날씨가 좋아졌음.

gloss.en: The weather improved after the storm passed.

lead: Rina tersenyum lebar dan langsung menelepon ibunya.
lines: Dia merasa sedih setelah mendapat kabar baik.

why.en: A big smile and she rings her mum right away after good news → she's happy.
why.ko: 좋은 소식 뒤 활짝 웃으며 바로 엄마에게 전화 → 기쁨.

gloss.en: She felt joyful after getting good news.

lead: Ada piring kotor dan sampah kertas di mana-mana di kamar itu.
lines: Kamarnya rapi setelah pesta kecil.

why.en: Dirty plates and paper everywhere after the party → the room is a mess.
why.ko: 파티 뒤 더러운 접시와 종이가 사방에 → 방이 엉망.

gloss.en: His room was messy after the small party.
gloss.ko: 작은 파티가 끝난 뒤 그의 방은 엉망이었다.

lead: Sekarang orang harus antre lama untuk mendapat meja di kafe itu.
lines: Kafe ini menjadi sepi setelah ulasan bagus.

why.en: People now queue for a table after a good review → the café got popular.
why.ko: 좋은 후기 뒤 이제 자리를 위해 줄을 섬 → 카페가 인기를 얻음.

gloss.en: This cafe became popular after good reviews.
gloss.ko: 이 카페는 좋은 후기 뒤에 인기가 많아졌다.

lead: Aku tinggal di Medan, dan sahabatku tinggal di Papua.
lines: Kami menjaga persahabatan meskipun dekat.

why.en: We live at opposite ends of the country → the friendship survives despite distance.
why.ko: 나라 양 끝에 삶 → 멀리 떨어져 있어도 우정을 지킴.

gloss.en: We keep our friendship even from afar.
gloss.ko: 우리는 멀리 떨어져 있어도 우정을 지킨다.

lead: Setelah bekerja dua belas jam, kaki Ani terasa berat sekali.
lines: Dia tetap tersenyum meskipun segar.

why.en: Twelve hours of work and heavy legs, yet she still smiles → she was tired.
why.ko: 열두 시간 일하고 다리가 무거운데도 웃음 → 피곤했음.

gloss.en: She kept smiling even though she was tired.

lead: Tangan Eko gemetar dan suaranya pelan sekali.
lines: Wawancara pertama Eko dengan menteri terasa santai karena dia gugup.

why.en: Shaking hands, a very quiet voice, and he was nervous → the interview felt stiff.
why.ko: 손이 떨리고 목소리가 아주 작고 긴장함 → 인터뷰가 딱딱했음.

gloss.en: Eko's first interview with the minister felt stiff because he was nervous.
gloss.ko: 에코의 장관과의 첫 인터뷰는 그가 긴장해서 딱딱하게 느껴졌다.

lead: Wati sudah mengecat sejak subuh, dan punggungnya pegal.
lines: Wati sudah segar, tapi masih ingin menyelesaikan pintu dapur hari ini.

why.en: Painting since dawn with an aching back, and 'but still wants to finish' → she was tired.
why.ko: 새벽부터 칠해서 허리가 쑤시고 '그래도 끝내고 싶다' → 피곤했음.

gloss.en: Wati is tired, but she still wants to finish the kitchen door today.
gloss.ko: 와티는 이미 지쳤지만 오늘 부엌문을 끝내고 싶다.

lead: Di pasar baru itu tidak ada dinding, hanya atap dan tiang.
lines: Bangunan pasar yang baru punya desain tertutup supaya udara mengalir.

why.en: No walls, only a roof and posts, so air can flow → the design is open.
why.ko: 벽 없이 지붕과 기둥만, 공기가 통하도록 → 열린 설계.

gloss.en: The new market building has an open design so the air can flow.
gloss.ko: 새 시장 건물은 공기가 통하도록 열린 설계로 되어 있다.

lead: Awan hitam tebal menutupi kota sejak kemarin.
lines: Budi berasumsi hujan akan turun minggu ini karena langit sudah cerah.

why.en: Thick black clouds over the city since yesterday → the sky is overcast, a sign of rain.
why.ko: 어제부터 짙은 먹구름이 도시를 덮음 → 하늘이 흐림, 비의 징조.

gloss.en: Budi assumed it would rain this week because the sky was already cloudy.
gloss.ko: 부디는 하늘이 이미 흐려서 이번 주에 비가 올 거라고 짐작했다.

lead: Kantor Budi sekarang tidak mau membayar tiket dan hotel untuk wartawan.
lines: Tahun ini anggaran ruang redaksi dipotong, jadi Budi sering liputan ke luar kota.

why.en: The budget was cut and the office won't pay for trips → he rarely travels for stories.
why.ko: 예산이 깎이고 회사가 출장비를 안 냄 → 취재 출장이 드묾.

gloss.en: This year the newsroom's budget was cut, so Budi rarely covers stories out of town.
gloss.ko: 올해 편집부 예산이 깎여서 부디는 다른 도시로 취재를 거의 가지 않는다.

lead: Sejak memasang aplikasi itu, Putri harus mengisi baterai ponselnya tiga kali sehari.
lines: Aplikasi itu mencatat aktivitas pengguna terus-menerus, jadi baterai lambat habis.

why.en: Constant tracking and charging three times a day → the battery drains fast.
why.ko: 쉬지 않는 기록과 하루 세 번 충전 → 배터리가 빨리 닳음.

gloss.en: The app records the user's activity constantly, so the battery drains fast.
gloss.ko: 그 앱은 사용자 활동을 계속 기록해서 배터리가 빨리 닳는다.

lead: Bayu terlalu asyik mengobrol sampai tidak melihat papan jalan.
lines: Bayu ingat berbelok di persimpangan, jadi mereka harus putar balik.

why.en: Too busy chatting to see the sign, and they had to turn back → he missed the turn.
why.ko: 수다에 빠져 표지판을 못 봤고 되돌아가야 함 → 꺾는 걸 놓침.

gloss.en: Bayu forgot to turn at the intersection, so they had to make a U-turn.
gloss.ko: 바유가 교차로에서 꺾는 걸 잊어서 그들은 차를 돌려야 했다.

lead: Di setiap pesta kampung, Rudi selalu jadi penari terbaik.
lines: Rudi malas menari dangdut, jadi tamu-tamu memintanya naik panggung.

why.en: The best dancer at every party, and guests ask him on stage → he's good at it and keen.
why.ko: 모든 잔치의 최고 춤꾼이고 손님들이 무대에 부름 → 잘 춤.

gloss.en: Rudi is great at dancing dangdut, so the guests asked him to get on stage.
gloss.ko: 루디는 당둣 춤을 잘 춰서 손님들이 그에게 무대에 올라 달라고 했다.

lead: Pagi itu puluhan karyawan antre di depan lift kantor Bayu.
lines: Kalau lift kosong, tangga adalah alternatif yang lebih cepat bagi Bayu.

why.en: Dozens queuing at the lift → the stairs are faster only when the lift is crowded.
why.ko: 엘리베이터 앞에 수십 명이 줄 섬 → 엘리베이터가 붐빌 때만 계단이 더 빠름.

gloss.en: When the elevator is full, the stairs are a faster alternative for Bayu.
gloss.ko: 엘리베이터가 꽉 차면 바유에게는 계단이 더 빠른 대안이다.

lead: Di ruangan itu ada musik keras dan anak-anak berteriak.
lines: Ruangan itu terlalu sepi untuk belajar.

why.en: Loud music and shouting children → the room is too noisy to study in.
why.ko: 시끄러운 음악과 소리치는 아이들 → 공부하기엔 너무 시끄러운 방.

gloss.en: That room is too noisy for studying.

lead: Hanya sepeda motor yang bisa lewat di gang itu.
lines: Gang di depan warung Lestari terlalu lebar untuk mobil.

why.en: Only motorbikes can get through → the alley is too narrow for a car.
why.ko: 오토바이만 지나갈 수 있음 → 차가 다니기엔 너무 좁은 골목.

gloss.en: The alley in front of Lestari's shop is too narrow for cars.
gloss.ko: 레스타리네 가게 앞 골목은 차가 다니기엔 너무 좁다.

lead: Rak-rak kulkas Ayu dipenuhi botol sampai pintunya sulit ditutup.
lines: Kulkas di toko Ayu sudah kosong dan tidak ada kapasitas lagi untuk minuman baru.

why.en: Shelves crammed with bottles so the door hardly shuts → the fridge is full.
why.ko: 병이 꽉 차서 문이 잘 안 닫힘 → 냉장고가 가득 참.

gloss.en: The fridge in Ayu's shop is full and has no more capacity for new drinks.
gloss.ko: 아유네 가게 냉장고는 이미 꽉 차서 새 음료를 넣을 자리가 없다.

lead: Hari itu air sungai bergerak cepat dan membawa batang-batang kayu.
lines: Eko sempat tergoda untuk berenang di sungai, tapi arusnya terlalu tenang.

why.en: The water was moving fast carrying logs, and 'but' explains why he didn't swim → the current was strong.
why.ko: 물이 빠르게 흐르며 통나무를 실어 감, '하지만'이 수영 안 한 이유 → 물살이 셌음.

gloss.en: Eko was tempted to swim in the river, but the current was too strong.
gloss.ko: 에코는 강에서 수영하고 싶었지만 물살이 너무 셌다.

lead: Tangan Ayu dingin dan dia terus melihat jam di dinding.
lines: Majalah lama tergeletak di meja ruang tunggu, tapi Ayu terlalu tenang untuk membacanya.

why.en: Cold hands and checking the clock again and again → she was too nervous to read.
why.ko: 손이 차갑고 계속 시계를 봄 → 읽기엔 너무 긴장함.

gloss.en: Old magazines lay on the waiting-room table, but Ayu was too nervous to read them.
gloss.ko: 대기실 탁자에 옛 잡지가 놓여 있었지만 아유는 너무 긴장해서 읽지 못했다.
